title: DNS picks the region and the balancer picks the VM
summary: A store sells to Mexico and Spain under a single domain, tienda.mx, from Querétaro and Madrid. If the primary region fails, shoppers must reach the other one within minutes.

requirements.1: {{s1}} publishes a single name, tienda.mx, and answers with region A's address while it is healthy, and otherwise with B's, with a 60 s TTL.
requirements.2: {{s2}} probes from several points on the internet, at a set interval, that each region's balancer answers; if one fails, slot 1 stops announcing it.
requirements.3: {{s3}} receives HTTPS in region A, terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the web VMs that pass their health check.
requirements.4: {{s4}} manages region A's web VMs as a group, spread across fault domains, and grows or shrinks with the load.
requirements.5: {{s5}} delivers the alarm's alert to the on-call team when slot 2 marks a region as down; the repair clock starts with that alert.
requirements.6: {{s6}} does in region B what slot 3 does in A: terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the healthy web VMs.
requirements.7: {{s7}} does what slot 4 does, for the web VMs in region B: manages them as a group and grows or shrinks with the load.

s1.explanation: Traffic Management steering policies serve DNS answers only for public DNS; the failover policy serves the primary answer first and uses Health Checks monitors to know whether its answers are healthy.
s1.hint_cue: answers with region A's address while it is healthy

s2.explanation: Health Checks monitors any public-facing service, such as an external load balancer, from vantage points around the world at intervals of 10 s or more, and the failover policy uses those monitors.
s2.hint_cue: probes from several points on the internet

s3.explanation: OCI Load Balancer terminates SSL on a listener, for example on port 443, with its certificate bundle, and spreads requests across the servers of a backend set, which has its own health check policy.

s4.explanation: An instance pool is a set of instances managed as a group from an instance configuration; with autoscaling it grows or shrinks by a metric or a schedule.
s4.hint_cue: grows or shrinks with the load

s5.explanation: Monitoring alarms publish their message to a Notifications topic when they change state, for example from OK to FIRING, and the topic delivers it to its subscriptions, such as PagerDuty.
s5.hint_cue: delivers the alarm's alert to the on-call team

s6.explanation: In region B another OCI Load Balancer terminates SSL on its listener and spreads requests across the servers of its backend set, by its health check policy.
s6.hint_cue: terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the healthy web VMs

s7.explanation: Region B has its own instance pool: with autoscaling it grows or shrinks and, when it scales in, balances the removals across fault domains.
s7.hint_cue: manages them as a group and grows or shrinks with the load

oci-dns-private-resolver.s1: The private resolver answers name queries inside VCNs, and the policies that pick answers by their health only exist for public DNS, not for private DNS.

oci-lb-health-check.s2: The backend set health check policy checks the servers behind the balancer; DNS policies judge the health of their answers with Health Checks monitors and probes, not with this policy.

oci-api-gateway.s3: API Gateway is for publishing APIs with private or public endpoints; this slot needs to terminate SSL on a listener and spread requests across the servers of a backend set.
oci-api-gateway.s6: API Gateway is for publishing APIs with private or public endpoints; this slot needs to terminate SSL on a listener and spread requests across the servers of a backend set.

oci-instance-configuration.s4: An instance configuration is the template with the image, shape and metadata to create instances; it does not manage a group or grow with the load.
oci-instance-configuration.s7: An instance configuration is the template with the image, shape and metadata to create instances; it does not manage a group or grow with the load.

oci-compute.s4: Each web VM in the diagram is already a Compute instance; the slot asks for the set that manages them as a group and grows or shrinks with the load.
oci-compute.s7: Each web VM in the diagram is already a Compute instance; the slot asks for the set that manages them as a group and grows or shrinks with the load.

oci-logging.s5: Logging gives access to the logs of the tenancy's resources so you can search and filter them; the alert reaches the on-call team through the service the alarm publishes its message to.
